title: Power-map differential and smooth local graph data
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p$ prime [def-weil-field], and let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $h:X\to X$ be a $k$-endomorphism and $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ a $k$-point with $h\circ x=x$. Assume that $x$ has an $h$-stable affine open neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], that $B$ is generated as a $k$-algebra by $t_1,\ldots,t_r$, and that $h^\#(t_i)=t_i^{p^n}$ for some integer $n\geq1$. On tangent spaces [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] one has $dh_x=0$ and $1-dh_x=1$, including when $x$ is singular. Under the canonical identification $T_{X\times_kX,(x,x)}\simeq T_{X,x}\oplus T_{X,x}$ [def-pc-fibre-product], the tangent images of the graph $(1,h)$ and the diagonal $(1,1)$ are respectively $\{(v,0):v\in T_{X,x}\}$ and $\{(v,v):v\in T_{X,x}\}$; they have zero intersection and their sum is the whole tangent space.
Suppose in addition that $x$ belongs to a smooth open $U\subseteq X$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and that the local ring of the equalizer $F=X\times_{X\times_kX,(1,h),\Delta_X}X$ at the point specified by $x$ is $k$ via its structural map. Put $d=\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. There exist affine open neighbourhoods $W\subseteq V\subseteq U$ of $x$ with $h(W)\subseteq V$. The open neighbourhood $W\times_kV$ of $(x,x)$ in $X\times_kX$ is smooth over $k$, and the graph of $h|_W:W\to V$ and of the inclusion $W\hookrightarrow V$ are closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] isomorphic to $W$. Write $A=\mathcal O_{X\times_kX,(x,x)}$, and let $I,J\subset A$ be the kernels of the stalk maps from $A$ to $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ induced respectively by these graph and diagonal maps. Then $A,A/I,A/J$ are regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme], with residue field $k$, and
$$\dim_kT_{X,x}=d,\quad\dim A=2d,\quad\dim(A/I)=\dim(A/J)=d,\quad I+J=\mathfrak m_A,\quad A/(I+J)\simeq k.$$
The last isomorphism identifies this quotient with the given equalizer local ring. No global separatedness is assumed.

proof.text: For the rational point x, the structural residue map k → κ(x) is bijective. The canonical residue-field point therefore equals x. The given fixed-point identity transports to this canonical point. Graph and diagonal carry x to the specified product point by the fibre-product universal property.

For a tangent vector v, the dual-number source has a closed point mapping to x, hence factors through the affine open O. Compare v followed by h with the zero tangent vector on sections of O. The maps agree on structural constants because both are over k, and their first dual-number coordinates agree because x is fixed. In characteristic p the second coordinate of a power a^(p^n) is zero for n ≥ 1, by the explicit square-zero power formula. The zero tangent vector also has zero second coordinate. The generator-closure hypothesis implies equality of ring maps, hence equality of the morphisms. Choose the zero linear map D, proving the required postcomposition formula and id-D=id.

Apply the rational product tangent-space equivalence and transport its base point from the canonical residue-field point to the specified x. Its projection formulas and the vanishing just proved show, by pullback hom-extensionality, the required graph and diagonal formulas. Injectivity of the equivalence gives the zero intersection; the identity (a,b)=(a-b,0)+(b,b) gives the sum assertion.

Smooth regularity on U and the stalk isomorphism of its open immersion imply regularity of O_X,x. Use the existing rational tangent/cotangent linear equivalence, equality of ranks under the bijective structural residue map, invariance of finrank under duality, and the regular-local cotangent dimension formula. Thus d=finrank_k T_X,x is a natural number equal to the Krull dimension of O_X,x.

Choose affine V containing x inside U, then affine W containing x inside V intersect h^(-1)(V). Restriction gives hW:W→V. The two graph maps into W×_k V are sections of its first projection. That projection is separated because V is affine over the affine base; consequently both sections are closed immersions. Smoothness is preserved by restriction, base change and composition. The canonical map W×_k V→X×_k X is an open immersion containing the rational product point, and smooth regularity transfers its stalk regularity to the ambient stalk A. Its residue field is k, since the displayed product point is a section over k. The product tangent equivalence and regular-local dimension formula give dim A=2d; no shrinking to constant relative dimension is needed.

The global graph and diagonal maps are sections of the first projection. Functoriality on stalks therefore gives right inverses to their stalk ring maps α,β:A→R, without assuming global separatedness. These maps are surjective. Take I=ker α and J=ker β and use the quotient-by-kernel ring equivalences to R. Regularity, dimension d and bijectivity of the structural residue maps transfer along these ring equivalences; structural compatibility follows from functoriality of the stalk maps.

Prove the local intersection quotient directly by universal properties. At the specified point w of the graph/diagonal pullback, the composite stalk map π:A→O_F,w kills I+J by the two pullback projections. Set Q=A/(I+J); it is a nonzero local ring because π factors through it. Surjectivity of α and β induces surjective local maps R→Q. Their spectra, followed by the canonical stalk-to-scheme maps, agree in the ambient scheme, so lift uniquely to F. This lift sends the closed point to w: the diagonal is a monomorphism and hence the first pullback projection is injective. The universal property of a local-ring spectrum then supplies a map O_F,w→Q. After precomposing with the quotient and using α,β surjective, the two composites are identities; equality of the scheme maps is checked on the pullback projections and by cancelling the canonical stalk-to-scheme monomorphisms. This gives the required eF with its prescribed values. Compose eF with the inverse of the assumed bijective structural map k→O_F,w to define eK. The kernel of the surjection A→Q→k is I+J, hence the unique maximal ideal of A. The final structural identity follows from the two inverse identities.

The delivery is one commit with the item and its report. It adds no new nodes. The statement is identical to the base (live and side-live are still unsplit). There is no repair note, so this is a first split. Nothing matches the SGA route-lock regex. Step 1 is genuinely elementary: the dual-number map t_i -> a_i+b_i eps goes to a_i^q=a_i (p|q, eps^2=0, fixed point), giving the zero vector, also at singular points. Step 2 uses 0BEB with the (v,0)/(v,v) decomposition. Step 3 uses 056S, then 0B2E duality, then the 00KU cotangent dimension to get dim T=d. Step 4 uses the rational-point stalk dimension node, then 02G1 local constancy, then the 01IT basis twice to get W in V∩h^{-1}V without assuming the intersection is affine. Step 5 uses 01VB/01VA permanence for relative dimension 2d, and regularity plus the product tangent to get dim A=2d. Step 6 uses P=C⊗D with surjective alpha and beta and the 01QO(2) single affine cover, so both graphs are closed without separatedness. Step 7 uses 01HV/01I1: A=P_q, and alpha_q is surjective since alpha(P∖q)=C∖m_C, so A/I≅R≅A/J. Step 8 gives the fibre-product ring P/K⊗P/L≅P/(K+L) as an open of F; localization exactness gives I+J, and the hypothesis O_F≅k gives I+J=m_A. Edge cases checked: d=0, k[t]/(t^2), affine space, imperfect k, non-separated X. Accepted tool_uses (generic AG tools from other units, all Lean-closed or Mathlib leaves, no cycle): 0BEB, 056S, 0B2E, 00KU, 00OU-node, 02G1, 01IT, 01VA/01VB, 01I4, 01QO, 01HV, 01I1. Implicit but acceptable: an open of a smooth scheme is smooth of the same local dimension.

lean.note: The helper declarations construct the canonical structural maps, graph, specified fixed point and stalk transports using the recorded fibre product and tangent space. The differential and product equivalence are characterized on dual-number morphisms, and the quotient identifications are characterized by the canonical stalk maps. The accepted Q42 stage-1 split is preserved verbatim.
